text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

*The company that manages Mozambique's Cahora Bassa dam, HCB-Hidroelectrica, lost 24 billion escudos in 1996, the chairman of the company said. This loss is 79 percent down on 1995 due to the apreciation of Mozambique's currency.
*Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said she intends to create a programme to modernise the metallurgy sector which she considers a high priority for Portugal.
*Banco Comercial Portugues seeks quotation on the Madrid stock exchange, bank chairman Jorge Jardim Goncalves said. He said the more markets the bank is quoted on, the more liquid the stock is.

*Continental/Mobil, based in Lousado, northern Portugal, will increase its capacity with the switching of production from other units of the German group Continental to Portugal and the Czech Republic.
*The state will sell its remaining 10 percent stake -- 350,000 shares -- in steel company Lusosider on the bourse on July 23 at 1,500 escudos per share.
*The group Pestana is one of the competitors to buy 55 percent of the Hotel Polana, in Maputo, Mozambique, presently held by South African group Karos.
